description:
Observed in examples/monte_carlo_rtp.exs (defk-9p6.17): `i = if pow2, do: band(v, n - 1), else: rem(v, n)` compiled as a select (both arms computed, README design decision 2 / select/4 in the compiler) cost 48 ns/spin, against 41.5 ns/spin for a plain `rem(v, n)`; a branch would have skipped the division. Also noted: a branch-free run count built from band/if selects was slower (45 ns/spin) than a `cond` that stops at the first mismatch (27 ns/spin).

Add a cost heuristic to `select?/1`: arms containing div, rem, or a float division (and later: loads, calls) are not speculated; they compile as branches. Measure on count_primes (which the select was introduced for, defk-jp3) that nothing regresses, and on the Monte Carlo example. Document in docs/language.md section 7 that an untaken arm may still be evaluated when it is cheap arithmetic, and is skipped when it contains a division.

Done when: the heuristic is in with a test on the generated C (a rem arm produces an if/else, an add arm a select), count_primes is unchanged within noise, and the example's index selection is simplified back to the if form.

comments.text: Heuristic in (branch defk-id9/select-cost-heuristic). Finding: integer div/rem were already never speculated (speculate? had no clause for them, so rem arm = if/else already); the only speculated division was float /, now removed. Array reads and calls are not speculated either; documented in docs/language.md s7. Measurements PROVISIONAL, taken under load from other agents. demo.exs count_primes(1M) defk yielding ms, 3 runs: before 197/202/205 (best 197), after 187/206/192 (best 187), plain C 183-199: unchanged within noise (generated C identical, the select is a count + 1). Monte Carlo example (3 runs, 100M spins): defk 446.7/455.3/507.0 ms, elixir 1418-1610 ms, 3.17x, correct true, verdict good. The example never had a pow2 select form (no hand rewrite in source or git log), so nothing to revert.

title: Select compilation evaluates both arms even when one contains div/rem: cost heuristic
